rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent dominant stepped mass across views, with the same core object legible in plan, axonometric, and elevations, so it clears the coherence gate. It is not merely a box: the terrace logic, cut corner, and lift/notch produce a readable hierarchy and a recognizable upper mass over a lighter base. The road-frontage response is present but somewhat conservative; the blue access edge is answered by a small underside opening/ground relief rather than a strongly public court, so void publicness is only moderate. For neighborhood living, the mass plausibly supports compact mixed neighborhood use: low-rise, capacity-aware, and street-oriented, with a legible active threshold. Sectionally it is decent but not exceptional; the stepped roof/profile is coherent, yet the public/entry void is not as forceful as the program brief suggests. The references mostly reinforce the same neighborhood/courtyard/terrace language, while the counterfactual supports the principle of a continuous sectional landform rather than a different typology.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise courtyard composition with connected wings and terraced circulation can support neighborhood-scale public living.
